accepted_edits.reason: the s13 heading, Why and done-when edits are exactly what findings naming-1 and reasoning-1 of r-20261116T232843557818 asked for

findings.reason: the worker is bound by the done-when, which names the actual endpoint, so the heading misleads a scanning reader but sends no node down a wrong path.
findings.text: the heading "Run scratch cannot fill the reservation node" states a capacity endpoint (the node never fills) while the done-when delivers only "a resumed run keeps the scratch its new step creates"; a reader of the plan index reading headings concludes the volume-filling defect of the old text is addressed, which no clause of §13 now measures

findings.reason: a repair aimed at the end-record reading leaves the incident intact when the pointer is the absent fact, and the plan's negative control ("restore the base settle predicate, and the resumed-step test finds its scratch removed") is satisfiable only by a fixture that withholds the resume's live pointer, i.e. a race, so the section must name which of the two facts the endpoint rests on before dispatch.
findings.text: the Why states that a resumed run "still carries the end record its earlier attempt wrote, so the settle its own new step runs can judge it over and remove the directory just made for it", but the predicate the same sentence cites puts the live-pointer test first and only the end record second: in `settle_run_scratch` (`reckon/crew/gc.py:1737-1748`) a run id present in `live_ids` is state RUN_SCRATCH_LIVE and is never removed, so the carried end record decides nothing while the resume's pointer is visible; the plan's own evidence says as much — a second resume at 19:38Z worked, and the preserved evidence directory holds `live-pointer-at-copy.json` — which means the deciding fact is whether the resumed run's live pointer is visible on the node at the instant its step settles, not that an end record survives
